title: Declarative Decision-Tree Evaluator
description: Evaluates a caller-supplied, hash-pinned decision tree against caller-supplied facts entirely offline, client-side. The tree is inert data -- one audited interpreter walks it over a closed operator set (eq, in, lt, lte, gt, gte, between, all_of, any_of, none_of); no eval, no expression strings, no function-valued criteria. Every node, internal criteria included and not leaves only, must carry a citation {clause, source, source_digest, snapshot_location}; a tree with any uncited node is rejected by the loader before evaluation. The tree's own declared tree_digest is never trusted as an oracle for itself: it is recomputed from the tree's canonicalized bytes and evaluation refuses to proceed on a mismatch. Bounds (max_depth=12, max_nodes=256, max_tree_bytes=64KiB) are declared and enforced, cycle-acyclicity is checked at load, and evaluation walks an explicit iterative pointer, never recursion. Ships with one demonstrator tree, the Reg D Rule 501(a) entity-type accredited-investor category test (17 CFR 230.501(a)(1)/(2)/(3)/(8)/(9)), enumerated exhaustively over its 5 declared boolean fields -- 32 combinations, 0 unexplained results -- because every criterion in that tree is a bounded enum. This is never a full accredited-investor determination: the natural-person prongs ((a)(4)-(a)(7), (a)(10)-(a)(13)) and every numeric-threshold test are explicitly out of the demonstrator's declared scope. The kernel itself carries no classification rules of its own; a caller must supply its own tree to get a different classification.

tree.description: The decision tree to evaluate, delivered as data (never baked into the kernel). Shape: {tree_id, tree_version, tree_digest, root, nodes}. Each node in `nodes` is {kind:'criterion', field, operator, operand, branches:{true, false}, citation} or {kind:'leaf', verdict, weight?, citation}. `tree_digest` must equal sha256(canonical-JSON(tree minus tree_digest)) or evaluation is refused. Every node must carry a non-empty citation {clause, source, source_digest, snapshot_location} or the tree is rejected by the loader.

tree_digest.description: sha256 hex digest of the canonicalized tree (this field excluded from what is hashed).

root.description: Node id of the root node.

nodes.description: Map of node id to node. Bounded: max_nodes=256, max_depth=12 root-to-leaf, max_tree_bytes=65536 (UTF-8 bytes of the whole tree object).

facts.description: Field values the tree's criteria are evaluated against. A criterion node whose declared `field` is absent from facts causes evaluation to refuse with FACT_FIELD_MISSING rather than silently branching.

mcp_tool_definition.name: evaluate_decision_tree
mcp_tool_definition.description: Evaluates a caller-supplied, citation-gated, hash-pinned decision tree against caller-supplied facts over a closed operator set (eq/in/lt/lte/gt/gte/between/all_of/any_of/none_of). Rejects any tree with an uncited node or a tree_digest that does not match its own recomputed bytes.

output_example.scope_note: This kernel is a generic decision-tree interpreter. It carries no embedded classification rules of its own -- every call must supply its own {tree, facts} in policy_parameters. Any citation, verdict, or bound reported below comes entirely from the caller-supplied tree, never from anything hardcoded in this kernel.
